items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: But I heard the tenor saxophone player, Dick Wilson. Fantastic tenor saxophone player. He's the first guy that I heard playing a major seventh chord.

ctx.x:
Terrell.
But I heard the tenor saxophone player, Dick Wilson. Fantastic tenor saxophone player. He's the first guy that I heard playing a major seventh chord. This was 1936. I heard him play that seventh chord on "Little Joe From Chicago." I said, "Wow, that note sounds strange!" And I dug around later on and found out what it was. I said, "How could get F-sharp in that G-chord," you know. But it sounded good. He put the F-sharp up there, you know, heh-heh...

Many kind of ways I learned lessons, you know. I was listening to Dizzy on the review one day, on the radio, Dizzy Gillespie, and he was saying how he learned about the minor seventh with the flat five in it; he learned it from Thelonious Monk in New York, and that's what they got together on the introduction to "Round About Midnight," you know. But I remember coming in contact with that chord back home. Because my cousin lived with us, and she was studying piano. Not that she wanted to; because the family wanted…
